photos.caption: Lake Tahoe, looking southwest. California Views No. 4, 1873 — the year Isabella Bird stopped at Tahoe on her way east.
Isabella Lucy Bird, English traveller and naturalist (1831–1904), who crossed Colorado on horseback in the autumn of 1873.
Head of the Saint Vrain, Rocky Mountains, Colorado, 1873 — the river Bird followed up into the front range.
photos.credit: William Henry Jackson / U.S. Geological Survey of the Territories

photos.caption: Long's Peak from Estes Park, Colorado, 1873 — photographed during the Hayden Survey the same season Bird arrived at Evans's cabin.
photos.credit: William Henry Jackson / U.S. Geological Survey of the Territories

photos.caption: Long's Peak from the lower end of Estes Park, 1873 — the 14,259-ft summit Bird climbed with Mountain Jim Nugent in early October.
photos.credit: William Henry Jackson / U.S. Geological Survey of the Territories

photos.caption: The Front Range of the Colorado Rockies, seen from Bald Mountain near Ward, 1873 — the country Bird rode through daily from Evans's ranch.
photos.credit: William Henry Jackson / U.S. Geological Survey of the Territories

photos.caption: Castle Rock, Boulder Canyon, Colorado, 1873 — typical of the canyons Bird picked her way through on the long November ride south.
photos.credit: William Henry Jackson / U.S. Geological Survey of the Territories

photos.caption: Long's Peak from Estes Park, 1873 — Bird's final view of the range before her December ride back across the plains.
photos.credit: William Henry Jackson / U.S. Geological Survey of the Territories
